# 🎙️ Podcast Script – The Aesthetic & Wellness Edge  
**Guest: Kristen Carbone – Founder, Subrosa Med Spa (Atlanta, GA)**  

---

### Intro  
**Bethany (Host):**  
Hi everyone, and welcome back to *The Aesthetic & Wellness Edge*! I’m your host, Bethany Gifford. After more than a decade working with surgeons, med spas, and wellness leaders, I now help practices uncover growth opportunities and scale smarter, not harder.  

Today’s guest is someone who embodies the word *disruptor* in the best possible way. She’s gone from makeup artistry to device sales and now runs one of Atlanta’s most unique med spas—Subrosa Med Spa. Known for its moody, speakeasy vibe and people-first culture, Subrosa is showing the industry that you can prioritize inclusivity, employee well-being, and profitability all at once.  

But first, a quick word from our sponsor.  
[**Sponsor Message Placeholder**]  

I’m thrilled to welcome Kristen Carbone, the founder of Subrosa Med Spa. Kristen, thank you so much for being here!  

---

### Conversation Flow  

#### Part 1 – The Journey  
- Kristen, take us back—your career began in beauty at just 19, working with MAC Cosmetics and weddings. What pulled you deeper into the medical aesthetics side?  
- You’ve worn so many hats—paramedical skincare, med spa and plastic surgery roles, then sales with Alma Lasers. What turning points or lessons along the way shaped your vision for Subrosa?  

#### Part 2 – Designing a Disruptive Space  
- Subrosa doesn’t look like a typical med spa. No beige. No white. No blue. What inspired the speakeasy, musician-themed design?  
- How do you think the vibe of a med spa influences not just clients, but staff culture as well?  

#### Part 3 – Culture & Team Building  
- You’ve made staff culture and retention a cornerstone—health insurance, fair pay, empowerment. Why was that so important to you from the beginning?  
- What have you learned about leadership and building a team that feels safe, supported, and motivated in this industry?  

#### Part 4 – Marketing & Growth  
- Atlanta is a competitive market. What strategies have you leaned into for growth—partnerships, local marketing, SEO, AI, or something else?  
- What have been your biggest wins so far, and what challenges have you faced in standing out?  

#### Part 5 – Industry Disruption & Inclusion  
- You’ve made inclusivity central to Subrosa—even offering support for gender-affirming transitions. Why does this matter so deeply to you?  
- How do you see the industry balancing inclusivity and innovation while still running profitable businesses?  

#### Part 6 – Looking Ahead  
- Where do you see Subrosa in 3–5 years?  
- Beyond your practice, what role do you hope to play in shaping the aesthetics industry as it evolves?  

---

### Closing  
**Bethany (Host):**  
Kristen, thank you for sharing your journey and the bold, people-first approach you’ve taken at Subrosa. I think your story is going to inspire a lot of providers to rethink how they build culture and community in their own practices.  

For our listeners—if you’re in the Atlanta area, definitely check out Subrosa Med Spa. We’ll have links in the show notes.  

Thanks for tuning into *The Aesthetic & Wellness Edge*. Be sure to subscribe so you don’t miss future conversations with the leaders redefining aesthetics and wellness. Until next time, keep growing smarter, not harder.  

---

Hi Kristen! I’m so excited to have you on The Aesthetic & Wellness Edge!
This primer will give you a quick overview of the podcast, your background as I’ll present it, and some guiding questions so our conversation flows smoothly. Nothing is scripted, the goal is a casual, engaging chat that highlights your story, philosophy, and impact in the aesthetic space. ✨

🌟 About Kristen Carbone & Subrosa Med Spa
Founder of Subrosa Med Spa, Atlanta, GA

Began her career in beauty at just 19 as a makeup artist (MAC Cosmetics & weddings), later pursuing a paramedical skin care degree.

Worked across med spas and plastic surgery practices before moving into device sales as a top rep for Alma Lasers, helping practices integrate cutting-edge technology.

Opened Subrosa, a moody, speakeasy-inspired med spa designed to break away from the industry’s standard “beige and white” look—every detail curated, down to treatment rooms named after musicians.

Known for building a values-driven culture: fair pay, health insurance, employee empowerment, and a safe, inclusive environment for all clients (including gender-affirming transitions).

Philosophy: Be a disruptor—show the industry that profitability and people-first culture can (and should) coexist.

Industry Disruption & Inclusion

How med spas can balance inclusivity, innovation, and profitability.

Future Vision
